reads.sell: Sauvignon Blanc from the upper Loire, grapefruit, lime and cut grass with a smoky, flinty edge, crisp and bone dry. Pour it with goat's cheese, shellfish or a herb crusted fish.

why.grape: Grapefruit and cut grass from pyrazines over high acid, with no oak and no cream, mark Sauvignon Blanc; the restraint and the gunflint place it in the Loire rather than Marlborough.
why.climate: Tart citrus, green herbaceous notes, high acidity and moderate alcohol say a cool continental site.

reads.sell: Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc, bursting with passion fruit, grapefruit and freshly cut grass, zesty, dry and unoaked. Serve it well chilled with oysters, a green salad or goat's cheese.

why.grape: Pungent passion fruit and grapefruit over cut grass and green pepper, with searing acid and no oak, is Sauvignon Blanc at full volume.
why.climate: High acidity and moderate alcohol beside intense, ripe tropical fruit say a cool, sunny maritime climate: long bright days for ripeness, cold nights to keep the acid.
